clue.text: Lofty under tree

parts.note: sub- is the Latin-derived prefix meaning under
the lime is a tree, also called the linden

explanation.surface: Something high up sits beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is exalted or elevated in thought or character, so lofty in spirit.

clue.text: Policy of TUC or some northern Ireland politicians

definitions.meaning: the Trades Union Congress stands for the principle of organised labour in trade unions
Ulster politicians who want to keep Northern Ireland in the UK hold this creed, so it stands for them collectively

explanation.surface: A question of what the trade unions or certain Ulster parties stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions; in Northern Ireland, Unionists want to stay part of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both support for trade unions and the political creed of keeping a union of states together.

clue.text: Capitalist?

parts.note: read not as an investor but as someone who lives in the capital city of England

explanation.surface: A one-word question about a believer in free markets.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Britain's capital is, whimsically, a capital-ist: a person of the capital.

clue.text: Way I state to be orderly

parts.note: a method is a way of doing something
taken as written
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone declares the right way to be tidy and systematic.
explanation.definitionFit: A methodical person works in a systematic, well-ordered manner.

clue.text: Ruler has another hour

indicators.note: another version of the word has means its letters arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A monarch is granted an extra hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges HAS to SHA, and H for hour follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran (Persia).

clue.text: A kiss and a cuddle would be low in school

indicators.note: in tells us the cow's word goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Canoodling would be frowned on at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for a cow's call, not 'not high'.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch is to kiss and cuddle amorously.

clue.text: Saw the digs disintegrate

indicators.note: to disintegrate is to break apart, so the letters of the two words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An archaeologist watches the excavation collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted is the past tense of sight, to catch sight of or see something.

clue.text: Crude, strange, Scottish ramshackle hut

parts.note: unco is a Scots word for strange or unusual

indicators.note: a ramshackle building is tumbledown and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rough, odd, tumbledown shack in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth means lacking manners or refinement, so crude in behaviour.

clue.text: Defend winning contestant

definitions.meaning: to support or speak up for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stand up for a cause; as a noun it is the winner of a title.

clue.text: Eminence of high official losing a right

indicators.note: losing means the following letters are dropped from the official's title

parts.note: a dignitary is a person holding a high office

explanation.surface: A grand functionary loses a privilege along with his standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes A and R from DIGNITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity is high rank or estimation, the stature that eminence also describes.

clue.text: Train in the nursery

parts.note: read not as teaching toddlers but as the childish imitative word for a steam locomotive

explanation.surface: Teaching toddlers in the playroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children call a railway engine by the sound it makes, a reduplicated nursery word.

clue.text: Is it bound to be a shopping list?

definitions.text: Is it bound to be a shopping list?

parts.words: Is it bound to be a shopping list?
parts.note: bound is read as stitched into covers, a bound book of goods to order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a list for the shops is inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail-order store's bound booklet lists all the goods on sale.

clue.text: Completely at home with drink, nothing else

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a tot is a small measure of spirits
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Staying in with just a drink and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: In toto is Latin for entirely or as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, entirely.

clue.text: Withdrawal of troops

definitions.meaning: aloofness or emotional distance from others
a body of soldiers sent away on a separate mission

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both aloofness and a group of soldiers detached for special duty.

clue.text: Go chatting round port

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Telling someone to go and do the rounds gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: Chittagong is the chief seaport of Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Chittagong is a major seaport on the Bay of Bengal in Bangladesh.

clue.text: Being the same forwards and backwards

indicators.note: the clue tells us the answer reads identically in both directions, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Describing something that is identical whichever way you look.
explanation.walkthrough: Esse is Latin for 'to be', used in English for existence or essential being.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is a philosophical term for existence or essence.

clue.text: Remembering about one's profession

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a calling is a vocation or profession

explanation.surface: Thinking back about one's line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalling means bringing back to mind, remembering.

clue.text: Inordinate rage before examination that's most extensive

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged anger ahead of the exam
inordinate means out of order or excessive, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Excessive fury before an exam that matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inordinate' rearranges RAGE to GREA, and 'before' puts it ahead of TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest is the superlative of great, meaning largest or most extensive.

clue.text: Romantic tangle?

parts.note: a love affair muddle is read literally as an ornamental knot symbolising love

explanation.surface: A complicated love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a decorative knot of ribbon given as a token of love, literally a tangle of romance.

clue.text: Height of shabby articles bound to go round

indicators.note: to go round means one word encircles the other

parts.note: bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: Ragged items bound to circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' here means certain, not tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural height.

clue.text: Building blocks we're told actor found in Devon

indicators.note: we're told signals that a word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: bricks are blocks used in building
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: Bricks and a performer turn up in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Brixham is a fishing town in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brixham is a harbour town on Tor Bay in the English county of Devon.

clue.text: Animal, marsupial initially needing space

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, an animal

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of marsupial

explanation.surface: A creature, a pouched mammal at that, needing room to roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space or capacity.

clue.text: Right cloth had been removed for this procession

indicators.note: removed means moved about, so the letters have been shifted out of place

explanation.surface: A suitable cloth was taken away for the parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A torchlight procession is a parade lit by flaming torches.

clue.text: Battered shoe filled with former sugar

indicators.note: filled with means the second piece goes inside the first
battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A worn-out shoe stuffed with old confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' rearranges SHOE to HOSE, and 'filled with' puts EX inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexose is a simple sugar with six carbon atoms, such as glucose.

clue.text: Surprised to find network hidden these days

indicators.note: hidden means one piece is tucked away inside the other

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era
a maze is a network of paths

explanation.surface: Astonished to discover a web concealed in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' tells us MAZE sits inside AD, not that the answer is in the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amazed is to be filled with wonder, astonished.

clue.text: One living abroad for financial reasons finds charge on former French island

definitions.text: One living abroad for financial reasons

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by government
ex means former
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: An expatriate is billed on a once-French isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax exile lives overseas to avoid high taxes at home.

clue.text: Burden youngster with energy

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Weighing down a boy with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To lade is an old word for to load, putting a burden on.

clue.text: Unidentified VIP?

parts.note: read as an unnamed person who is also, in the idiom, an important figure

explanation.surface: An anonymous celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unspecified person, and also a person of importance, as in 'he thinks he's somebody'.

clue.text: Composition

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Composition (8)' only: a bare definition with no wordplay, apparently cut short; search found no fuller text

clue.text: One who stirs up public interest no end — excitedly referring to notes

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the stirrer's title is dropped

parts.words: One who stirs up public interest
parts.note: an agitator campaigns to rouse public feeling

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser without limits gets worked up over music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the final R of AGITATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning play in an agitated, restless manner.
